long_biography.plain_text:
Charles F. Willis IV built his career around a then-unconventional idea: airlines could lease spare jet engines independently from the aircraft they powered. He began at Alaska Airlines while his father was the airline's president, giving him valuable industry access. After sales and marketing roles, he established an aviation consultancy and equipment-trading business that became Willis Lease Finance Corporation.

Under Willis, the company grew into a global engine-leasing and aviation-services platform. It combined operating leases with engine-sharing pools, parts distribution, fleet management, technical consultancy and maintenance support, giving airlines alternatives to owning costly spare equipment. Willis served as president and chief executive for decades before becoming executive chairman, continuing to shape the company's long-term strategy.

uncertainties.detail: The yacht-owner identity does not rest on name similarity. Steamship Mutual and the Coast Guard identify Willis Lease Marine LLC with Fabulous Character; an SEC subsidiary exhibit connects that exact entity to WLFC; official WLFC and SEC records identify Charles F. Willis, IV as the founder and current Executive Chairman.

Willis founded the principal wealth-producing company and no reviewed source shows that he inherited it. His direct historical account says he began in aviation with his father, who was president of Alaska Airlines, establishing meaningful status, access and industry experience. The evidence does not show that his father supplied the company's capital or transferred a material operating asset.

The current SEC proxy establishes substantial continuing beneficial ownership and official sources establish Willis's current Executive Chairman role. Aviation & Aerospace is therefore clear, but point-in-time ownership percentages are deliberately omitted from the biographies because they can change.

The immutable record stores Charles F. in first_name and Willis, IV in last_name. Official records consistently show Charles as the given name and F. as the middle initial, so the dossier proposes those two supported structured-field changes while retaining the accurate display form. The suffix remains embedded in the existing last-name field because optional suffix proposals are outside the strict dossier contract.

Reviewed company, SEC and interview sources did not establish an exact birth date, birthplace, secondary nationality or secondary residence. Focused searches did not verify a dedicated personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website; only the canonical company website is proposed.

Aviation is the minimum useful approved active tag and directly satisfies its material-wealth and defining-operating mandate. The catalogue contains no narrower aircraft-engine-leasing tag, and Aerospace would overstate the evidence because WLFC is an aviation-finance and services business rather than an aerospace manufacturer.

The existing biography is dominated by vessel ownership, explicit source attribution and a point-in-time claim about family shareholdings. The replacement preserves the durable founder and aviation-business facts while removing transient yacht and ownership-detail material.

The biographies omit vessel details, market values, current ownership percentages, unverified net-worth estimates, private-family material and unsupported birth details. No live or compiled change is authorised.
